newsitem.title: UK: Modest UK traffic reduction bill makes progress.
newsitem.headline: Modest UK traffic reduction bill makes progress.

text.p: A bill that would require local councils to set targets for reducing traffic congestion cleared its first parliamentary hurdle on Friday with all-party support.
The measure, sponsored by Liberal Democrat MP Don Foster, now stands a good chance of becoming law although the government says it will seek changes when the bill is debated in committee.
The bill aims to to encourage better public transport, cycling and walking, pedestrian-only zones and traffic calming measures.
"It is not an anti-car bill," Foster said. "It is an anti-excessive-traffic bill."
Junior transport minister John Watts welcomed the bill for seeking to set local, not national, targets.

"I support the idea that local authorities should review the case for setting targets. I see this as a natural development of strategically reviewing transport pressures which authorities already undertake when they compile their bids for funding each year," Watts said.
"There are a number of elements where we believe further consideration on the bill will be needed. But I am sure we have a basis on which we can agree," he added.
Foster said there was growing pressure in Britain for action to curb congestion, which he said was costing business billions of pounds as well as exacerbating pollution and health problems.
"If we can do something about these problems we can save lives, improve the environment and save billion of pounds for the nation," Foster said.
